name: Street Corn Chicken Rice Bowl

ingredients.buy: 2/3 cup crumbled; 1/2 cup crumbled, for topping
juice and zest of 3 1/2 limes; 7 tablespoons
1/2 cup chopped; 2/3 cup chopped; 1 1/2 cups leaves, for topping

writer_notes: All 20 locked ingredients are used by a step; no step uses anything not on the buy list.
Sea Salt is intentionally used twice (chicken spice blend and rice) per the locked two-amount buy string, and is kept separate from the 'Salt' line used in the corn salad.

Cotija (2/3 cup salad + 1/2 cup topping), Fresh Cilantro (1/2 cup rice, 2/3 cup salad, 1 1/2 cups topping), and Lime Juice/Zest (corn salad + rice + finishing squeeze) each split across multiple steps; prose reflects every use.
Red Onion locked as fresh sliced for topping; the transcription offered pickled or fresh, prose uses fresh to match the buy string.

Tokens used: {{cal}}, {{protein}}, ${{cost_ps}}. 'under 600 calories' and 'over 40 grams' are literal bounds only. No cost_lines were provided, so shop_smart makes no per-line or comparative price claims and references only locked buy quantities.
Method facts retained verbatim from the transcription: 165F internal temp, ~20 min rice simmer, 4 to 5 min per side. These are cooking facts, not macros or costs.

Data sanity: 597 cal and 44.6 g protein both in band; chicken 4 3/4 lb / 14 = ~0.34 lb raw per serving is consistent with the protein figure; corn, avocado, cotija, and rice quantities all scale sensibly for 14 servings. No smells found. Source named avocado-oil mayo but the locked commodity is generic Mayonnaise, noted for the record only.

prose.intro_html:
Mexican street corn, elote, is one of those flavors that tastes like a splurge and costs like a side dish. We took that creamy, tangy, lime-and-cotija corn and built a whole dinner around it: seasoned chicken breast, cilantro lime rice, and a generous scoop of that street corn salad on top. It lands at {{cal}} calories and {{protein}} grams of protein a serving, which clears our 40 gram bar with room to spare and still comes in under 600 calories.

Here is the honest part. This is a bowl you would happily pay twelve dollars for at a fast-casual counter, and we are making fourteen of them out of one skillet, one pot, and a mixing bowl. That is the whole game.
prose.shop_smart:
Canned corn carries this recipe. You need 7 cups drained, roughly four standard cans, and canned corn is one of those pantry items whose price barely moves through the year. Drain it well so the salad stays thick instead of soupy.

Chicken breast is your big line. You need 4 3/4 pounds, so buy it in the largest pack you will actually cook through and cut it into 1-inch chunks at home instead of paying for pre-cut. A knife and five minutes is the whole difference.

The spice rack does most of the flavor work: chili powder, cumin, smoked paprika, garlic powder, and onion powder. If your store has bulk bins, the same spoonfuls come out to a lot less than the little branded jars. Cotija is the one specialty cheese, and you use it twice, 2/3 cup stirred into the salad and 1/2 cup crumbled on top, so plan for a little over a cup total when you pick up your wedge.

Greek yogurt does the work sour cream would in a classic elote, and you only need 1 3/4 cups out of a big tub. Round out the cart in produce with limes, a couple of jalapenos, cilantro, avocado, and a red onion, and you are done.
prose.make_it:
Start the rice, because it takes the longest. Bring the water to a boil, stir in the rice and sea salt, then cover, drop the heat to low, and let it simmer about 20 minutes until tender. While it is still warm, fold in the chopped cilantro, lime juice, and lime zest so the rice drinks it all in.

Make the street corn salad. In a big bowl, combine the drained corn, Greek yogurt, cotija, mayonnaise, lime juice and zest, the diced jalapeno if you want the heat, cilantro, and a little salt. Stir gently until it comes together, then taste and adjust. Set it aside so the flavors get acquainted.

Season the chicken. Mix the chili powder, cumin, smoked paprika, garlic powder, onion powder, and sea salt in a small bowl, then toss the 1-inch chicken chunks with the blend until every piece is coated.

Cook the chicken. Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium. Once it is hot, add the chicken and cook 4 to 5 minutes per side until it is cooked through and the internal temperature reaches 165 degrees. Work in batches if the pan gets crowded, because crowded chicken steams instead of browning.

Build the bowls. Lay down the cilantro lime rice, top with the chicken, add a generous scoop of the street corn, then finish with cubed avocado, red onion, more cilantro, a sprinkle of cotija, and a squeeze of lime.
prose.portion_html:
Fourteen containers is the target, and the honest way to hit it evenly is to weigh, not eyeball. Once the rice, chicken, and corn salad are all cooked, weigh each one and divide by fourteen so every container gets the same base. A kitchen scale turns guesswork into fourteen identical bowls, which is exactly what you want when the whole point is knowing your macros.

Lay the rice down first, then an even share of chicken, then a scoop of street corn. Hold the avocado, red onion, cilantro, and the topping cotija until serving day so the avocado does not brown and the cilantro stays bright. Each finished bowl lands at {{cal}} calories with {{protein}} grams of protein.
prose.cost_closing_html: Here is what all of that adds up to: ${{cost_ps}} per serving for a bowl that tastes like the twelve dollar version at the counter. Fourteen dinners, real chicken, real produce, and a street corn salad that never once tastes like a diet.
prose.upsell_html: Cook once, eat all week, and let the math work for you. When a home-built bowl runs ${{cost_ps}} and the fast-casual version runs north of ten dollars, that gap is your grocery budget quietly winning. Thrifty Crew membership is a dollar a month, and one recipe like this covers a year of it many times over.

steps: Bring the water to a boil, add the rice and sea salt, then cover and simmer on low about 20 minutes until tender. Fold the chopped cilantro, lime juice, and lime zest into the warm rice.
In a large bowl, combine the drained corn, Greek yogurt, cotija, mayonnaise, lime juice and zest, diced jalapeno if using, cilantro, and salt. Stir gently, taste, adjust, and set aside.
Mix the chili powder, cumin, smoked paprika, garlic powder, onion powder, and sea salt, then toss the 1-inch chicken chunks in the blend until fully coated.
Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium. Add the chicken and cook 4 to 5 minutes per side until cooked through and 165 degrees internal, working in batches if the pan is crowded.
Divide the cilantro lime rice among the containers, top with chicken and a scoop of street corn, and finish with avocado, red onion, cilantro, cotija, and a squeeze of lime.
